02The pressure points

Where compliance slows the business down.

Financial institutions tend to meet the same pressure points, whatever their size or stage of growth.

  • An inspection is announcedThe regulator expects evidence, structure and quick answers, while the team is already at maximum capacity.
  • Audit findings keep piling upRecommendations stay open, deadlines slip, and remediation competes with day-to-day work.
  • Growth outpaces the frameworkNew products, markets and volumes arrive before the controls, tooling and team are ready.
  • Compliance is seen as a brakeThe business experiences compliance as a list of refusals instead of a partner in its decisions. Compliance teams struggle to adapt to their changing environment, or business teams struggle to understand the compliance risks.
See how we help

06Background · Meet our Managing Director

Sophyan Belataris

With a decade of experience across payments, electronic money, retail banking and private banking, Sophyan has built his career at the intersection of regulation, operational reality and business transformation.

Connect on LinkedIn

Over the years, he has developed a pragmatic and business-oriented approach to compliance, supporting regulated financial institutions in navigating increasingly complex regulatory environments without losing sight of performance, scalability and strategic objectives.

For Sophyan, compliance should never be reduced to a simple control function or a regulatory burden. When properly designed and integrated, it becomes a true business enabler: strengthening resilience, facilitating growth, building trust and creating long-term competitive advantage.

His approach combines regulatory expertise, adaptability and execution with a strong commitment to ethics, integrity and sustainable development. Whether supporting governance structures, enhancing AML frameworks or helping organisations adapt to evolving payment regulations, his focus remains the same: delivering actionable solutions that align compliance requirements with operational efficiency.

Today, he is particularly engaged in helping organisations structure, scale and transform their compliance functions in a way that supports both regulatory expectations and business ambitions.

Privacy notice

SPX Consulting takes the protection of your personal data seriously. This notice explains which personal data we process when you visit this website or contact us, why we do so, and what rights you have under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Belgian data protection law.

1. Who is responsible for your data

The controller is SPX Consulting (VAT BE1012171244), represented by its Managing Director, Sophyan Belataris. For any question about this notice or your personal data, write to sb@spxconsulting.com. Given the size and activities of SPX Consulting, no Data Protection Officer has been appointed; the Managing Director handles all privacy requests personally.

2. Which data we process, why, and on what basis

When you contact us by email
Your name, email address, organisation, role and the content of your message. We use them to answer your request and, where relevant, to prepare a proposal. Legal basis: steps taken at your request before entering into a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR), or our legitimate interest in answering professional enquiries (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
When you book a meeting
Meetings are booked through Google Calendar appointment scheduling. Google collects your name, email address and chosen time slot on our behalf, and we receive them to hold the meeting. Legal basis: steps taken at your request before entering into a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
When we work together
Contact details of your representatives, engagement documents, invoices and correspondence. Legal basis: performance of our contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and compliance with our accounting and tax obligations (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR).
When you visit the website
Technical data generated by your browser, such as IP address, date and time of the request, pages requested and browser type, recorded in our host's server logs to deliver the site and keep it secure. Legal basis: our legitimate interest in operating a secure website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

We do not use your data for profiling or automated decision-making, we do not sell it, and we do not send unsolicited marketing messages.

3. Who receives your data

Your data is only shared with service providers that help us run our activity, acting on our instructions or under their own terms where they act as independent controllers:

  • our website host (OVHcloud, servers located in the European Union);
  • Google, for email, calendar and appointment booking;
  • our accountant and, where required by law, public authorities.

Links to LinkedIn and Le Figaro take you to third-party websites that apply their own privacy policies.

4. Transfers outside the European Economic Area

Some Google services may involve the transfer of data to the United States. These transfers rely on the EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework, under which Google LLC is certified, and on the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses.

5. How long we keep your data

  • Enquiries that do not lead to an engagement: up to 3 years after our last exchange.
  • Client and engagement records: for the duration of the engagement, then for the period required by Belgian accounting and tax law (currently up to 10 years for accounting records).
  • Server logs: for a short period set by our host, no longer than 12 months.

6. Your rights

You may at any time ask to access your personal data, have it corrected or erased, restrict or object to its processing, and receive it in a portable format. Where processing relies on your consent, you may withdraw it at any time. Send your request to sb@spxconsulting.com; we will answer within one month and may ask you to confirm your identity.

If you believe your rights have not been respected, you may lodge a complaint with the Belgian Data Protection Authority (Autorité de protection des données / Gegevensbeschermingsautoriteit), Rue de la Presse 35, 1000 Brussels, www.dataprotectionauthority.be.

7. Security

We apply technical and organisational measures appropriate to the nature of the data, including encrypted connections (HTTPS), access restricted to the Managing Director, and reputable service providers.

8. Changes to this notice

We may update this notice to reflect changes in our activities or in the law. The date at the top shows the latest version.

Cookie notice

This website is designed to respect your privacy: it does not use analytics, advertising or social media tracking cookies, and it does not follow you across other websites. That is why no cookie banner asks for your consent.

1. What cookies are

Cookies are small text files that a website stores on your device. Similar technologies, such as your browser's local storage, work in a comparable way. Under the ePrivacy rules applicable in Belgium, only those that are strictly necessary may be used without your consent.

2. What this website uses

Cookies
None. SPX Consulting does not place any cookie on your device.
Local storage and tracking
None. The website stores nothing on your device, uses no analytics or advertising tools, and loads its typefaces from our own server, so no third party is contacted when you browse it.

3. Third-party services you may choose to use

When you click to book a meeting, to visit our LinkedIn profile or to read the Le Figaro article, you leave this website. Google, LinkedIn and Le Figaro may then place their own cookies, under their own cookie policies, which we do not control.

4. Managing cookies

You can block or delete cookies and local storage at any time from your browser settings. Doing so will not prevent you from using this website.

5. Changes and contact

If we ever introduce cookies that require your consent, for instance to measure audience, we will ask for it beforehand and update this notice. For any question, write to sb@spxconsulting.com. More information on how we handle personal data is available in our privacy notice.
